SCOPE UPDATE 2026-10-26 (owner decisions Q15 and Q17; review findings C2 and F8). PR #3526 merged the bootstrap, but the review in a cloud session cannot reach the gateway: the tailnet is reachable only through the userspace proxy on 127.0.0.1:1055, local.py reachable() does not use it, and the reviewer environment allowlist (commands.py:13,60-62) drops proxy variables, so cloud make pr-open always refuses. Remaining work, on top of oracle-review-driver-local-20261026: the local adapter passes the proxy recorded in the bootstrap marker (gateway_proxy) to the reachability check and to the reviewer process only, never to git, uv or gh; the cloud socket directory is created with mktemp or verified owned by the user before tailscaled starts (today a predictable path plus an ignored chmod failure could hand the auth key to another local user's socket on a shared /tmp); TYPESAFE_API_KEY is documented as a required cloud environment variable (Q17). The live acceptance needs a Claude cloud session the owner launches when asked (Q15). Codex Cloud stays deferred.

Decision gate (owner accepted the residual 2026-10-26): in that session, test whether the reviewer can read TYPESAFE_API_KEY, the oracle-cloud gateway token and TS_AUTHKEY from any ancestor's environment, and record the result. The owner accepted those three as readable (compensating controls: oracle-cloud quota and revoke, the tagged ACL-limited Tailscale key, the classify-only TypeSafe key). If anything else sensitive is readable (for example a GitHub token), stop and ask.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, code) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Before publishing run make docs-reference-inventory-check, make doc-contracts-guard and make pr-preflight, and self-review with the code review action, fixing every Critical and Required finding. Publish only with make pr-open: never gh pr create, a raw push-and-open, or a PR-body override line; if make pr-open refuses, stop and report the exact refusal instead of routing around it. Until oracle-omp-pin-single-source-20261026 merges, make pr-open may run only with PATH prefixed by the darwin-arm64 omp 18.12.1 build recorded in that item (SHA-256 fa41b27d434380e99b713e4f9ced0f73eb1fc0c409fdf23a57c119971d24bac5, from https://build.stencil.so/d/omp/20261017-231446-291e055/omp-darwin-arm64), verified with shasum immediately before use; never any other side-loaded omp. Close out only with oracle SHIP on the exact head, every oracle thread answered (reply naming the fixing SHA, then resolve) and make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge or a ruleset or settings change, and never a stand-in, adjudication or backoff reset unless the owner names the PR and head (and the finding) in the current request after an Owner instruction comment. Never edit, delete, dismiss or minimise an oracle review, review comment or commit status, and never post a commit status by hand. Run /oracle-review only on a pending or absent head, or after a Dispute: reply with file:line counter-evidence; never to re-roll a decided head. Do not close, reopen, rerun or rebase other PRs. Until oracle-gateway-cloud-builder-access-20261025 merges, publish only from the owner's Mac. Rollback: if a change to the verdict or gate workflows or to the local review breaks its first live run after merge in a way that blocks other PRs, stop, run make trunk-revert PR=<n>, and report to the owner, who chooses between an absence stand-in and the broken-oracle-gate procedure. Never print tokens, keys, or the gateway URL or hostname; never spend model quota outside the review harness. Owner decisions are recorded in context and in the decisions file; a step that would contradict one stops and asks the owner.

Original description follows.

Problem: cloud builders (Claude Code on the web, Codex Cloud; docs/agent/cloud-builder.md) publish with make pr-open (cloud-builder.md:109). Once the local pre-PR review blocks pr-open until it can run, a session that cannot reach the gateway on the owner's Mac (127.0.0.1:4000) cannot open PRs. Owner decision 2026-10-25: give cloud builders gateway access over the tailnet with a cloud-scoped client token, rather than exempting them or stopping cloud publishing.

Outcome: a cloud session whose environment carries the cloud credentials joins the tailnet as tag:oracle-cloud and reaches only the gateway (https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:4000, already served by tailscale serve; docs/internal/oracle-gateway-host.md:22) with a third gateway client, oracle-cloud, added through the mechanism of oracle-gateway-named-clients-20261025. make cloud-bootstrap starts tailscaled in userspace-networking mode with in-memory state when the credential is present, and exposes the tailnet to the review through a local proxy (SOCKS5 or HTTP) if userspace mode requires it. Without the credential, bootstrap still succeeds and reports that the gateway is unavailable. With it, bootstrap also installs the OMP build that CI's reviewers use (the pinned version and checksum in .github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml) and verifies it, because the local review runs that harness; gate 1 also records the network allowlist entry its download needs.

Decision gates:
1. Feasibility, before owner setup: in a real Claude Code on the web session and a real Codex Cloud session, test whether tailscaled can run in userspace mode and reach controlplane.tailscale.com and a DERP relay under each platform's network settings, using a throwaway ephemeral key on a test tag the owner creates, or by documenting the exact network allowlist entries each platform needs. Record the result per platform. If a platform cannot reach the tailnet at all, stop and ask the owner (options: exempt that platform with a notice, or stop cloud publishing there).
2. Owner-only setup (settings and secrets): (a) tailnet policy: tagOwners for tag:oracle-cloud and one accept rule from tag:oracle-cloud to oracle-gateway:4000 only, mirroring tag:oracle-ci (oracle-gateway-host.md:43-54); (b) a Tailscale credential for cloud sessions: an ephemeral, pre-approved auth key tagged tag:oracle-cloud with an expiry, or an OAuth client limited to that tag; (c) cloud environment settings on each platform: ORACLE_GATEWAY_URL, the oracle-cloud token and the Tailscale credential, plus any network allowlist entries from gate 1. Write exact step-by-step instructions, block this item with that reason, ask the owner once, and resume when they confirm. The agent creates the oracle-cloud gateway client and its token file on the host.
3. Rotation: document how to rotate and revoke the oracle-cloud token and the Tailscale credential without touching oracle-ci or oracle-local.

Item guardrails: no change to tag:oracle-ci, the CI secrets, the oracle environment or the gateway bind; the cloud credential is ephemeral, tagged, and can reach only the gateway port; tokens never enter the repository, logs, PR bodies or tracker text; the agent edits no tailnet policy or cloud settings itself unless the owner supplies an API credential for that purpose in the current request; no paid cloud resources.

Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, comments) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Run make docs-reference-inventory-check and make doc-contracts-guard in addition to make pr-preflight. Close out with make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge, never a stand-in or bypass on these oracle soundness paths.
